item.text:
**3B.5 Research Note**

Overall read: Lula’s 2024 record is more consistent with **narrow, statutory, and rights-framed controls** than with emergency powers as a tool of intimidation. The main caveat is that these formal safeguards coexisted with continued police abuse on the ground.

- [Portaria MJSP nº 648, de 28 de maio de 2024](http://dspace.mj.gov.br/handle/1/12967) — Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública — 2024-05-28 — claim: established national body-camera rules for public security agencies, with audiovisual recording and oversight aimed at transparency, evidence preservation, and tighter control of police conduct. — IDs: 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1
- [MJSP lança diagnóstico sobre o uso de câmeras corporais pelos agentes de segurança pública](https://www.gov.br/mj/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/mjsp-lanca-diagnostico-sobre-o-uso-de-cameras-corporais-pelos-agentes-de-seguranca-publica) — Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública — 2024-07-31 — claim: the ministry published an evidence review linking body cameras to more reporting and lower police lethality, signaling a preference for monitoring over intimidation. — IDs: 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1
- [Decreto nº 12.341, de 23 de dezembro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/decreto/d12341.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-12-23 — claim: Lula regulated police use of force and less-lethal tools, explicitly citing legality, precaution, necessity, due process, and non-discrimination. — IDs: 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1
- [Decreto nº 12.167, de 6 de setembro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/decreto/d12167.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-09-06 — claim: authorized Armed Forces deployment for election security only for specified localities and periods defined by the electoral court, which is a bounded lawful use of emergency-style security powers. — IDs: 3B.5
- [GLO em portos e aeroportos é prorrogada pelo presidente Lula por 30 dias](https://www.gov.br/portos-e-aeroportos/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/2024/05/glo-em-portos-e-aeroportos-e-prorrogada-pelo-presidente-lula-por-30-dias) — Ministério de Portos e Aeroportos — 2024-05-06 — claim: Lula extended a GLO deployment for ports and airports in coordination with civilian authorities, and the operation was described in terms of inspections, seizures, and coordinated security rather than open-ended coercion. — IDs: 3B.5
- [Lei nº 14.967, de 9 de setembro de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/lei/l14967.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-09-09 — claim: created a national framework for private security and financial-institution security under federal police authorization and oversight, with administrative sanctions and due-process framing. — IDs: 3B.5
- [Decreto nº 12.006, de 24 de abril de 2024](https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2023-2026/2024/decreto/d12006.htm) — Presidência da República / Planalto — 2024-04-24 — claim: integrated school-violence reporting into national security information channels and an emergency number, a targeted administrative-control measure rather than broad surveillance. — IDs: 3B.5
- [Brazil: Comply with Rulings on Police Violence](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/15/brazil-comply-rulings-police-violence) — Human Rights Watch — 2024-03-15 — claim: HRW said Brazil still had not fully implemented independent-investigation requirements for police killings and that lethal police raids continued, showing that abuse-control systems remained incomplete. — IDs: 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1
- [World Report 2025: Brazil](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/brazil) — Human Rights Watch — 2025-01-01 — claim: covering 2024, HRW reported continued police killings and prison conditions marked by overcrowding and ill-treatment/torture, which is strong counterevidence that formal controls fully solved the abuse problem. — IDs: 3B.5, 3B.4, 3B.1

Search gap: I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Lula used emergency powers, security laws, surveillance, or anti-terror tools for collective punishment, intimidation, or generalized social control. The evidence I found is mostly bounded, legalistic, and rights-framed, but its effectiveness was uneven because police abuse and detention-abuse problems persisted.
